chain.label: Black hole night approach over unlit forest
chain.trigger: The night visual approach to runway 9 at TLH was conducted over a protected national forest area that was devoid of ground lights or other visible references

chain.label: Captain and first officer fatigued
chain.trigger: the captain was likely impaired by fatigue... the first officer's schedule and his reported difficulty adapting to frequently changing sleep cycles were conducive to the development of fatigue impairment

chain.label: FAA color vision screening/SODA inadequate
chain.trigger: the FALANT screening test, which is an approved color vision screening method for aeromedical certification, failed to identify the first officer's severe color vision deficiency

chain.label: First officer's severe congenital deuteranomaly
chain.trigger: all test results were consistent with a congenital severe deuteranomaly... the red lights would not appear to be red at all

caused_by.evidence: he was again issued the certificate with a SODA for the color vision deficiency... based on your operational experience

chain.label: Captain and flight engineer lacked black hole/CFIT training
chain.trigger: The captain and flight engineer had not received FedEx's CFIT avoidance/black hole training

chain.label: Late change of landing runway from 27 (ILS) to 9 (no vertical guidance)
chain.trigger: About 0528:26, the first officer asked, 'we ever decide if we're goin' nine or two seven?' The captain responded, 'yeah, we can do nine if you want to.'

caused_by.evidence: For an experienced captain to support a decision to change landing runways... suggests degraded decision-making consistent with the effects of fatigue

chain.label: Black hole visual illusion of being higher than actual
chain.trigger: pilots conducting visual approaches at night over terrain with minimal visible ground features or lighting often perceive the airplane to be higher than its actual altitude

caused_by.evidence: the approach to runway 9 at TLH (which was flown over unlighted terrain and in night visual conditions) resulted in black hole conditions
FedEx records indicate that the captain and flight engineer had not received this training

chain.label: First officer misread the all-red PAPI glidepath signal
chain.trigger: the first officer suffered from a severe color vision deficiency that made it difficult for him to correctly identify the color of the PAPI signal during the below-glidepath, nighttime, visual approach

caused_by.evidence: it is possible in this case that the red lights of a PAPI could have been identified as 'yellow' at lower light levels or 'white' when the light was brighter
the PAPI lights were the only reliable source of glidepath information in the black hole approach environment leading to runway 9
lower levels of illumination would further degrade such a pilot's ability to discern colors

chain.label: Failure to establish and maintain proper glidepath; steep low-power descent
chain.trigger: descending through 500 feet agl at a vertical speed of 1,248 feet per minute... with engine power settings of about 1.17 EPR

caused_by.evidence: the first officer did fly a concave approach, with a steeper-than-normal initial descent, which is characteristic of a black hole approach
PAPI lights... should have been, but were not, effectively used to maintain an appropriate glidepath by the first officer
his failure to maintain appropriate engine EPR settings during the approach, and his failure to respond to PAPI guidance that indicated the airplane was extremely low

chain.label: Captain and flight engineer failed to monitor the approach
chain.trigger: the captain and flight engineer failed to recognize the solid red PAPI display... and take action to correct the low approach

caused_by.evidence: the captain was likely impaired by fatigue and this impairment contributed to his degraded performance (especially in the areas of crew coordination and monitoring)
the captain decided, at the first officer's suggestion, to change the landing runway... during the somewhat hurried final approach that ensued

chain.label: Unstable approach continued instead of mandatory go-around
chain.trigger: the captain announced that the approach was 'stable'... the accident approach was not stabilized as the airplane descended through 500 feet agl and... the pilots should have detected this and performed a go-around

caused_by.evidence: its rate of descent was greater than FedEx's recommended 1,000 fpm, the engines' power settings were less than the expected 1.3 to 1.45 EPR, and its glidepath was low
The flight engineer's failure to adequately monitor the approach... removed the last defense against the accident
one of the common deficiencies observed in fatigue-related accidents is a tendency to continue an approach despite indications that the approach should be discontinued

chain.label: Collision with trees short of runway 9
chain.trigger: The airplane collided with trees in a right-wing-low, slightly nose-up attitude during the approach to runway 9

caused_by.evidence: the first officer did not modify the steepness of the approach path in time, and the airplane collided with trees and terrain
if the approach end of the runway became obscured at any time during the visual approach, the pilots should have performed a go-around

chain.label: Ground impact and postcrash fire, airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: then impacted the ground, coming to rest on a heading of 260º... A postimpact fire ensued

caused_by.evidence: The airplane first impacted trees about 50 feet above the ground... The first evidence of ground impact was located near the edge of the wooded area

chain.label: Three flight crewmembers seriously injured
chain.trigger: The captain, first officer, and flight engineer were seriously injured

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was destroyed by impact and resulting fire... the three flight crewmembers received serious injuries
